subject: Clarifying hour-resolution for audit snapshot and bridge options
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Dawson <alicia.dawson@dawsonaudit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-12 09:15 -0700
Subject: Clarifying hour-resolution for audit snapshot and bridge options

Alicia —

Quick question as we prepare evidence for ClientCorp's SOC 2 Type II intake: the auditor checklist asks for a "point-in-time snapshot" for 2027-09. Our ingestion pipeline writes event logs with second-level UTC timestamps and rotates backups at 00:00:00 UTC. Two clarifications would help us avoid off-by-one issues when we hand off manifests:

1) For a snapshot labeled as "2027-09-30 (EOD)", do you treat 23:59:59 UTC as inclusive, or do your procedures consider the timestamp at 00:00:00 on 2027-10-01 as part of the prior day?
2) We can produce an hourly manifest (CSV) showing counts and first/last event timestamps for each hour. Would an auditor-signed manifest with SHA256 be acceptable as primary evidence for a point-in-time capture, or do you require raw log files for the exact second?

If a bridge letter is needed for any partial-day coverage, is there preferred language we should propose? I can share a sample manifest (sanitized) and a proposed wording if useful.

Thanks — trying to be explicit so the controls team produces the right artifact.

Jonas
Senior Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_log_manifest_sample.csv (stub)

From: Alicia Dawson <alicia.dawson@dawsonaudit.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Liu <emma.liu@clientcorp.com>
Date: 2027-10-12 12:34 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarifying hour-resolution for audit snapshot and bridge options

Jonas —

Good questions; short answers first, then specifics:

1) Our SOC 2 Type II evidence collection treats a point-in-time labeled as an "end-of-day" snapshot to include events up to and including 23:59:59 UTC. Events stamped exactly at 00:00:00 on the next calendar day are considered outside that snapshot unless explicitly documented as part of the prior-day rollforward.

2) We accept a signed manifest with hourly buckets as supporting evidence provided it: (a) lists first/last event timestamps per bucket, (b) includes counts, and (c) is accompanied by a verifiable checksum (SHA256) and a brief statement from the custodian describing the extraction method. Raw logs are preferred for deep forensic work, but for control testing a robust manifest + checksum is commonly sufficient.

Bridge letter: Yes, a short bridge will suffice when the organization cannot produce raw second-level files for a particular window. Recommended items in the bridge: scope/date range, reason for bridge (e.g., backup rotation), assertion that controls were operating as designed, and the window being covered with explicit timezone. We can co-sign language if ClientCorp requires auditor acknowledgment.

If you can share the sanitized manifest and the timezone for your backup rotation (you mentioned UTC, just confirming), I can draft a short template bridge we typically use and flag any language auditors prefer to see. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if helpful.

Best,
Alicia Dawson
Senior Manager, Dawson Audit Partners

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Dawson <alicia.dawson@dawsonaudit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-12 14:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying hour-resolution for audit snapshot and bridge options

Thanks, Alicia — that's helpful. Confirming details from our side before we produce artifacts:

- All primary event logs are stored in UTC; our daily backup snapshot procedure starts at 00:00:00 UTC and a small set of housekeeping jobs occasionally write late-arriving events for the previous day within the first 30 seconds after midnight (rare, but we want to be explicit).
- We'll prepare an hourly manifest for 2027-09-30 with the following columns: hour_bucket_start, hour_bucket_end, event_count, first_event_timestamp, last_event_timestamp, extraction_method, custodian_name.
- We'll compute a SHA256 checksum of the manifest file and provide that value and a short custodian statement.

Attachment: redwood_log_manifest_sample.csv (sanitized example).

Two follow-ups: Can you confirm whether the bridge statement should explicitly call out the "rare late-arriving writes within the first 30 seconds of UTC day N+1" phrase? Also, if you draft a template, could you include one sentence that states "auditor acceptance of manifest as sufficient evidence for control testing" or is that overreaching?

Jonas

From: Alicia Dawson <alicia.dawson@dawsonaudit.com>

Cc: Emma Liu <emma.liu@clientcorp.com>
Date: 2027-10-13 09:18 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarifying hour-resolution for audit snapshot and bridge options

Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks for the details. A couple of practical notes based on what you described:

- Please do call out the "rare late-arriving writes within the first 30 seconds of UTC day N+1" in the custodian statement. That transparency is helpful.
- We should avoid language that implies the auditor "accepts" evidence as definitive for all testing. Instead, I'm happy to state: "Based on review of the manifest and checksum provided by the company, auditor performed control testing using the manifest as supporting evidence for the selected sample dates." That phrasing is conservative but conveys that testing used the manifest.
- I've placed a short draft bridge letter in the linked Drive folder with two options: (A) limited scope bridge for housekeeping writes; (B) broader bridge covering a planned retention migration. Option A is the one I'd recommend here.

I'll also need a SHA256 and the extraction command (e.g., the script name or query) used to produce the CSV. If you prefer a quick sync, I have 20-min in the afternoons 3–4pm ET tomorrow.

Best,
Alicia

Attachment: draft_bridge_letter.docx (in Drive)

2) Jonas, please upload the manifest and SHA256 to the Drive folder Alicia shared and paste the link into HubSpot ticket HS-8421 once complete.
3) If Alicia is available, let's take the 20-min sync tomorrow at 3:30pm ET to confirm wording in Option A of the draft bridge letter. Alicia — can you confirm?

Thanks — Marissa
